title: Security & Governance — Where It Stands
thesis: Most security stacks are a bag of primitives; Softanza's is a doctrine. One capability lattice (effectful, sensing, compute, inference) and three postures gate every dangerous act uniformly, so an LLM actor holding inference only is refused a secret, a file write or a deployment by construction. On top sit a full identity stack (OIDC, SAML, WebAuthn, both sides) and an engine-computed tamper-evident audit ledger; the gaps are a unified injection-defense surface, the unbuilt plugin governance, and the absence of a formal threat-model document.

lanes.note: One capability lattice (effectful/sensing/compute/inference) and three postures enforce six checkpoints; agents rehearse in a stzVirtualFileSystem twin
stzAuth sessions, TOTP, WebAuthn passkeys, OIDC client and provider, SAML SP and IdP, HMAC request signing with nonce replay cache; ~417 guarded assertions
stzSecurityLedger over seclog.zig: a bounded hash-chained ring whose digest is computed in-engine; seal-to-file, verify names a broken link
crypto.zig ships SHA-256, HMAC, PBKDF2, constant-time compare, CSPRNG, TOTP, ES256/RS256; RSA/X.509 via vendored mbedTLS; no AEAD, no Argon2
stzSecretStore is the one governed door: every Reveal(name, actor) is gated and audited, secrets self-redact; no real backend adapter ships
stzSecurityGraph answers ReachesEffectful, BlastRadius and PathExists, catching multi-hop escalation; only three security rules ship
stzSecurityEvent is a typed record with a MITRE ATT&CK field and OCSF JSON export; redaction is enforced at construction; no PII/DLP surface
stzDetection -> stzSecuritySentinel -> stzIncident -> stzResponsePlan -> stzSecurityDrill; three detection shapes, no anomaly/ML, no Sigma interop
lanes.proof: stzSecurityDrill (adversary emulation vs a real spawned app)

lanes.note: stzSecurityAttestation makes a custody statement over a sealed ledger; export is a sensing act an LLM may not perform; no in-toto interop yet
mTLS and TLS ride vendored mbedTLS with a smoke guard and fuzz_tls.zig; no cert-lifecycle management, OCSP or cipher-policy governance
Primitives exist scattered (HTML/URL escaping in encode.zig, XXE closed by the XML parser); no unified validation surface, no SQLi/CSRF/XSS toolkit
A designed doctrine ('a plugin is a governed foreign capability') with a plan and comparative study; base/plugin is not loaded in stzBase.ring

standouts: A governance doctrine enforced uniformly: an LLM actor holding only inference is refused by construction, not by a rule someone remembered to write
An engine-computed tamper-evident audit ledger (hash-chained, seal and verify)
A full identity stack: OIDC, SAML and WebAuthn on both sides
Multi-hop escalation caught by graph reachability (ReachesEffectful, BlastRadius)
gaps: A unified injection-defense surface (the OWASP Top-10 core)
Authenticated symmetric encryption (AES-GCM / ChaCha20-Poly1305) and a modern KDF (Argon2)
A formal threat model mapped to guards
Plugin / foreign-capability governance, plus a shipped Vault/KMS backend adapter
